subject: MontclairHealth VPC upgrade: control-plane connectivity interruption and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@montclairhealth.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@montclairhealth.com>, infra@montclairhealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 22:14:00 -0700
Subject: Control plane connectivity after private VPC upgrade - impact

Sergio —

We ran the scheduled private VPC upgrade window last night (02:00–03:00 local). Around 02:12 we started seeing a spike of 503/connection errors from your inference endpoints for roughly 18–22 minutes. Our monitoring shows failed requests across three services (patient-index, notes-parser, and encounter-embeddings).

We pulled a few sample traces and attached a client-side event snapshot (client_event_snapshot_0828.zip) to this message. The errors correlate with repeated control-plane handshakes that timed out; calls that previously were 60–80ms jumped to 2–4s and then failed. This caused a number of retries and backpressure on our side.

Can you share:
- Immediate explanation of what changed during the upgrade window
- Whether this was a known fallback/rollback and why it lasted ~20m
- Short-term mitigation we can apply while you investigate

This incident impacted several productive workflows; our ops and compliance teams will need a short timeline and evidence for our audit.

Thanks — please escalate.

Alex Turner
SRE Lead, Montclair Health
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@montclairhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@montclairhealth.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 22:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control plane connectivity after private VPC upgrade - impact

Alex — thank you for the alert and the attached snapshot. I’m very sorry for the disruption.

Short answers up front:
- We initiated a maintenance for the private control plane (kernel upgrade + routing policy refresh) at 02:00. An unexpected orchestration leader re-election coupled with a partial auth broker timeout caused repeated handshake failures from 02:11–02:29. That produced the 503s you saw.
- We performed an automatic canary rollback at 02:30 which restored normal handshakes by 02:33. Total customer-facing impact window ~18–22 minutes.
- Immediate mitigation: we pushed an emergency config that pins leader-election timeouts and disabled the new routing policy for your tenant. We’ve also increased canary aggressiveness for future rollouts.

I’m pulling the control-plane logs and an initial postmortem draft now; I’ll send those within the hour. If you’re available I can join a short bridge at 09:00 PT tomorrow to walk through the timeline and evidence.

We’ll also include artifacts you can use for your audit (timestamps, log slices, and the rollback command).

Apologies again — we take these incidents seriously.

– Sergio Alvarez
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

Folks — forwarding Montclair's report and Sergio's ack. Summary of what we need before the customer bridge:

1) control-plane leader-election trace (02:00–02:40) + election timestamps
2) auth-broker timeout histograms and stack traces for the failing brokers
3) Canary rollback command and timing (who triggered, cluster id)
4) Evidence that tenant routing policy was disabled and timestamped

Preliminary notes from ops: the rollback was automated by the orchestration policy when the canary crossed 15% error rate; however the controller did not clear the old routing policy fast enough and that produced a second wave of handshake failures. That explains the 20m tail.

Let's get artifacts into: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-montclair-postmortem-draft and draft a short blameless timeline. Sergio, loop me into the bridge.

— Grace

Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Montclair Health — incident summary and draft postmortem (attached)

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for raising this. Attached is a short draft postmortem (montclair_postmortem_draft.pdf) and the extracted control plane logs (controlplane-logs-20260828.txt). Key points:

Root cause (short): during the scheduled kernel+policy upgrade, an orchestration leader re-election coincided with an auth-broker threadpool starvation on three nodes. That produced transient handshake timeouts. The automation rollback executed at 02:30 but stale routing policy state led to a 12–15 minute tail where some agents retried against partial control-plane state, extending the customer impact window to ~18–22 minutes.

Mitigations (implemented):
- Pinned leader-election backoff to 1s/3s windows in the 02:05 emergency patch
- Disabled the new routing policy for Montclair tenant at 02:17 (manual override)
- Increased canary abort sensitivity and fixed controller race that prevented dirty-state cleanup

Planned follow-ups (by priority):
1) Engineering to complete controller fix and deploy by 2026-09-02 (INF-5239)
2) Ops to add a cross-tenant canary guardrail and a faster routing-policy convergence healthcheck (ETA 2026-09-07)
3) We will provide the log bundle and signed timeline for your audit by 2026-09-03

Compensation: we acknowledge the production impact and would like to discuss a one-off service credit for the affected window. I’ll propose an amount on the bridge.

Next step: short bridge to review the artifact pack and compliance evidence — does 09:00 PT tomorrow work?

Attachment: montclair_postmortem_draft.pdf

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
